questions.q: Which function loads a CSV file into a pandas DataFrame?
questions.explain: pd.read_csv() reads a CSV path (or file-like object such as io.StringIO) and returns a DataFrame.

questions.q: info() shows amount with 7 non-null values in a DataFrame of 8 entries. What does that tell you?
options: One value in the amount column is missing
The amount column contains seven distinct values
questions.explain: Non-null count lower than the entry count means missing values. Here one amount is missing.

questions.q: After loading, info() shows order_date has dtype object. What does this usually mean?
options: pandas stored the dates as a special compressed type
The dates are still plain text and were not parsed into real datetimes
The column contains Python objects such as classes
questions.explain: By default read_csv leaves date-like columns as text (object). Use parse_dates to convert them.

options: The total of all amounts in the table
The sum of every numeric column
The count of missing values in each column
questions.explain: isna() flags missing values as True, and sum() counts the Trues per column.

questions.q: You have a very large CSV and only want to explore its structure quickly. Which read_csv option helps?
options: nrows, to read only the first few rows
questions.explain: nrows limits how many rows are read, so you can explore a huge file without loading all of it.
